title: Decoding Fast-Fail Framework: lightweight prober routing, multi-signal acceptance, and soft-fallback policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Add a lightweight, low-overhead speculative decoding framework that probes candidate model variants with a tiny prefill/fast-fail pass and decides whether to continue on the fast path or gracefully fall back to a full decode. This ticket covers the initial runtime adapters, acceptance signal definition, a soft-fallback policy, and an integration test harness. Motivation: reduce tail latency for common short/high-confidence responses while avoiding quality regressions and keeping per-token cost within acceptable bounds. Constraints: probes must not add >3ms median latency for warm requests, additional GPU memory use per request must be <1MB on average, and fallbacks must succeed without request duplication visible to callers. This is a runtime-side feature; model training is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Framework can route requests to a lightweight prober model variant (same architecture, smaller kv/quantization profile) and record acceptance signals
Define and compute a 3-signal acceptance score (prefix-match confidence, token-logit entropy delta, and kernel-latency delta) and expose as telemetry
If acceptance score >= threshold, continue fast-path decode with cached KV re-use; otherwise initiate soft fallback that resumes decode on full model without user-visible duplication

End-to-end e2e latency improvement: 50th percentile <= baseline and 95th percentile reduced by >= 10% for traffic shapes with avg tokens <= 25 (when probes used), with overall hosting cost delta <= +5%

Fallback success: for 1000 randomized test prompts, fallback path produces output with BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity >= 0.98 of baseline full-decode outputs where baseline is full model on same input
Rollout controls: feature flag to disable speculative path per-customer and per-route; metric dashboards for acceptance rate, fallback rate, and false-accept rate
Integration tests: synthetic harness that simulates KV-cold, KV-warm, and multitoken bursts exists and runs in CI
implementation_notes: Adapter layer in runtime: implement ProberSession wrapper that runs a short prefill (<= 4 tokens) on a quantized/fast-kernel variant and collects three signals

Signals: (1) prefix confidence (sum of top-1 logits normalized by length), (2) entropy_delta between prober and small sampled full model logits (approximated via calibration table), (3) kernel_latency_ratio (prober kernel vs expected full-kernel cost) - blend via weighted sum with decay

Kernel-aware scoring: use per-device kernel fingerprint to upweight probes run on incompatible kernels (reduces false accepts when kernel mismatch probable), store small kernel-fingerprint table in runtime
KV-cache warmup budget: reserve a short window (configurable ms) to transfer/rehydrate KV to full model on fallback; where possible snapshot prober KV to speed resume
Soft-fallback mechanism: orchestrator starts full-decode in paused mode if acceptance uncertain; upon fallback decision, swap internal token stream and resume without replaying user-facing tokens
Backpressure and throttling: global token budget limiter to avoid probe explosion under bursty traffic; per-route sample rate configurable
Config knobs: probe_length, acceptance_threshold, probe_variant, probe_sample_rate, kv_warmup_window_ms
Testing: unit tests for scoring math, fuzz tests for race conditions between prober and fallback, e2e perf test harness against local CUDA setup
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: enable at 1% traffic in staging cluster with probe_variant=quant-2bit and probe_length=3; run 72h and verify metrics
2) Canary: expand to 5% in production non-critical tenants; monitor acceptance_rate and false_accepts; enforce kill-switch if false_accepts > 1% over 1h
3) Tiered opt-in: expose per-customer feature flag; start with PLG customers who opted in; collect cost/latency delta per-customer
4) Full roll: 100% default-off; flip default on only after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and e2e quality gates satisfied
5) Post-roll: run nightly re-eval job that compares probe outputs vs full-decode baselines and surfaces drift alerts
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: probes introduce additional overhead and increase tail latency under heavy load. Mitigation: implement global probe budget and backoff; default probe_sample_rate low; add adaptive suppression when GPU utilization>threshold
Risk: false accepts causing quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative acceptance threshold, multi-signal fusion, per-route safelists (routes that never use probe), rapid rollback kill-switch
Risk: KV snapshot/resume complexity causing correctness bugs. Mitigation: start with non-snapshot resume (replay) for first release, then optimize to snapshot flow after stability
Risk: telemetry noise leading to bad threshold tuning. Mitigation: calibrate thresholds offline with corpora, add canary with synthetic prompts and label set
